newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, 30-year near par with U.S.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, 30-year near par with U.S.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing, boosted by foreign buying and spread-narrowing trades placed at the long end, analysts said.

"We're seeing some support from European outflows based on the EMU uncertainty," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN AMRO Bank Canada. "The 30-year spread now is basically zero, which looks precarious."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.46 to C$114.52 to yield 6.852 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.84 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to an all-time low of one basis point from six basis points at Monday's close.
"We're up a lot but down a lot from the highs. I think there's been a little bit of domestic buying, a little bit of foreign buying," said one Toronto-based bond dealer.

Analysts said the Canadian market was largely focused on whether the yield on Canada's 30-year bond would trade below the U.S. yield. Many market watchers predicted it could happen as early as today because of positive sentiment regarding the country's economic fundamentals.
While the Canadian 30-year bond traded to yield at parity with the U.S. 30-year late in the afternoon, if failed to break through the key level.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.14 to C$106.50 to yield 6.358 percent, while the U.S. 10-year fell 7/32 to 6.57 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 21 basis points from 16 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.93 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.03 percent.
